known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: UNODC SHERLOC (a UN-maintained legislative database) attributes an added closing sentence to this article via Royal Decree M/54 (22/7/1436H): 'ويجوز تضمين الحكم الصادر بتحديد العقوبة النص على نشر ملخصه على نفقة المحكوم عليه في صحيفة أو أكثر من الصحف المحلية أو في أي وسيلة أخرى مناسبة، وذلك بحسب نوع الجريمة المرتكبة، وجسامتها، وتأثيرها، على أن يكون النشر بعد اكتساب الحكم الصفة النهائية.' This sentence is ABSENT from all three sources cross-verified for this track (BOE portal, WIPO Lex/CITC PDF, MOF certified copy) and from the administering regulator's own current text. A dedicated follow-up research pass could not locate primary confirmation (Umm Al-Qura Gazette text or a working BOE amendments page) either way; the cited clause is also a boilerplate formula reused across other unrelated Saudi laws, suggesting possible misattribution. NOT included in this track's article text pending independent primary-source confirmation.

verification_methodology_note: DISTINCT VERIFICATION TIER, but the STRONGEST used anywhere in this corpus outside the primary MOJ-portal pipeline: full EXHAUSTIVE (not spot-check) article-by-article cross-verification across THREE independent sources, all matching word-for-word on all 16 articles. (1) PRIMARY: the Bureau of Experts (BOE) legal portal at laws.boe.gov.sa, LawDetails GUID 25df73d6-0f49-4dc5-b010-a9a700f2ec1d, reached via the WebFetch/curl method through an https://r.jina.ai/<url> reader-proxy prefix (direct sandbox network access to laws.boe.gov.sa is blocked at the TLS handshake/WAF level). (2) WIPO Lex (details/14570), hosting the CITC (Communications and Information Technology Commission) Official Translation Department's Arabic source PDF (a genuinely different production pipeline/host than BOE) at https://wipolex-res.wipo.int/edocs/lexdocs/laws/ar/sa/sa047ar.pdf, committed at inputs/anti_cyber_crime_source_pdfs/anti_cyber_crime_law_wipo_lex_sa047.pdf. (3) The Saudi Ministry of Finance regulations library, a scanned, officially stamped certified copy (visible seals of the Bureau of Experts, the Council of Ministers Presidency Diwan, and the Administrative Communications Center on every page), committed at inputs/anti_cyber_crime_source_pdfs/anti_cyber_crime_law_mof_certified.pdf. Both PDFs have no usable text layer (broken font cmap / pure scans); both were rendered to page images and read visually/OCR'd. A possible amendment to Article 6 (cited by the UN's UNODC SHERLOC legislative database, attributed to Royal Decree M/54 dated 22/7/1436H) was investigated via a dedicated follow-up research pass: the BOE portal (Saudi Arabia's own authoritative current-law database) does NOT show this addition, nor does the CITC regulator's own PDF (the body that administers this exact law); no primary confirmation (Umm Al-Qura Gazette text or a working BOE amendments sub-page) could be located either way despite genuine effort; the specific added clause is also a boilerplate formula reused across multiple unrelated Saudi laws, raising a real possibility of misattribution by whichever secondary source originated the UNODC claim. Given the two most authoritative sources checked (BOE and the administering regulator CITC) both show NO such amendment, this track presents Article 6 as verified by all three primary sources and does NOT include the UNODC-cited addition; the investigated-and-unconfirmed claim is preserved here rather than silently dropped. Separately, a minor Gregorian-date-gloss discrepancy was noted: the BOE portal's own page states the decree's Gregorian equivalent as 27/03/2007, while WIPO Lex, the MOF PDF's cover metadata, and general secondary sources uniformly give 26 March 2007 for 8/3/1428H; the Hijri date itself (8/3/1428H) is not in dispute and is what this track's decree_date_hijri field records.
